newsitem.title: SPAIN: BCH team seen favoured in Spain's Retevision bid.
newsitem.headline: BCH team seen favoured in Spain's Retevision bid.

text.p: The odds are on Banco Central Hispano's team to win the fight for a 60 percent stake of Retevision, which will become Spain's second basic phone operator by the end of the year, analysts said on Monday.
"If I were to bet, I'd bet for the consortium led by BCH," a Madrid-based foreign trading company's analyst said.
Earlier on Monday, the deadline for official expressions of interest, two groups said they would bid for Retevision, which will compete with just privatised Telefonica de Espana.
One consortium, led by Spain's BCH, groups France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and U.S. Sprint.
The competitor is made up of the Italian public holding STET, Spanish electricity group Endesa and Union Fenosa, and with the Basque group Euskatel.

A surprise, last-minute candidate was Germany's Mannesmann AG, the second mobile phone operator in Germany. Retevision was unable to say whether Mannesmann's bid was independent or was part of a consortium.
"BCH has partners which are strong in technology. Stet does not have much experience in international business," an analyst said.
Another analyst said that BCH, whose group made its interest public weeks ago, appeared more thought out in its approach.
"The BCH group seems more stable, the other is giving the impression of being a last-minute alliance," an analyst said.
The BCH club's sole problem seems to be a reduced cable network compared with competitors, industry analysts said.
In the STET consortium, Endesa and Union Fenosa will contribute 10,000 km of fiber optic networks for immediate use as an alternative telecoms network to Telefonica.
To help compensate, the BCH group announced on Monday a deal with Spanish railways Renfe which opens the door to using its fiber optic network to strengthen the consortium's bid.
But the crucial factor in winning the 60 percent Retevision stake will be the price the two groups offer, analysts said.
In mid-March, Retevision's board approved the conditions for the sale of a 60 percent stake in the firm for a minimum price of 45.6 billion pesetas.
The bidder will be obliged to underwrite a 10 percent capital increase in the firm, with a further payment of at least 25.3 billion pesetas.
"The groups' real interest will be reflected in the price," a foreign firm analyst said.
The period for presentation of bids ends on June 9, and the auction will be resolved in 60 days.
Nevertheless, the government is planning to privatise another tranche of Endesa in the Autumn, and its failure to win the Retevision contest might harm its image.
"If Endesa should gain the control of Retevision, that will boost further its privatisation this fall," said an analyst.
Analysts added that the forthcoming winner of the auction will be a natural ally of Airtel, the actual competitor of Telefonica in the mobile telephone sector.
"It will be logical that the second telephone operator in basic phones looks for a deal with the second mobile phone operator," said a source close to one of the two bidders.
